catalog.name: Sodexo UEM Packaging Guidelines Rules
catalog.purpose: Convert Sodexo packaging guidelines into measurable controls for Intune application governance, quality review and future web-based compliance scoring.

control_type.automatic: Can be checked from Intune, Graph API, CSV export, audit logs or repository metadata.
control_type.semi_automatic: Can be pre-filled from data but requires human confirmation.
control_type.manual: Requires documented evidence, governance validation or packaging review.

severity.critical: Can block packaging, deployment or compliance approval.
severity.high: Creates operational, security or lifecycle risk and should be remediated.
severity.medium: Quality or standardization gap to be corrected during normal governance.

rules.title: Business justification is mandatory
rules.requirement: Every application request must include a clear business or functional justification before packaging starts.

source.section: Application Pre-Validation / Business & Functional Validation

evaluation.pass: Business justification is documented and validated.
evaluation.partial: Business justification exists but lacks validation or clarity.
evaluation.fail: No clear business or functional justification is available.

rules.remediation: Request the business justification from the requester or reject the packaging request.

rules.title: Business and technical owners are identified
rules.requirement: The application must have designated business and technical owners.

source.section: Application Pre-Validation / Business & Functional Validation

evaluation.pass: Business and technical owners are present.
evaluation.partial: Only one owner type is documented or the owner naming is ambiguous.
evaluation.fail: No application owner is documented.

rules.remediation: Define the owner taxonomy and update the intake record and Intune metadata.

rules.title: Duplicate functionality is assessed
rules.requirement: The request must check whether the application duplicates an existing corporate tool. Consolidation must be prioritized when duplication exists.

source.section: Application Pre-Validation / Business & Functional Validation

evaluation.pass: No duplicate is found or consolidation decision is documented.
evaluation.partial: Potential duplicate exists but is not fully qualified.
evaluation.fail: Duplicate functionality is present with no documented decision.

rules.remediation: Compare with the application catalog and document whether to package, consolidate or reject.

rules.title: Preferred application model is considered
rules.requirement: The request must evaluate web app first, Microsoft Store second, and Win32 packaging only when no better option is available.

source.section: Application Pre-Validation / Application Type Prioritization

evaluation.pass: Preferred model assessment is documented.
evaluation.partial: Assessment is incomplete but packaging rationale exists.
evaluation.fail: Win32 packaging is requested without model assessment.

rules.remediation: Document why web or Store delivery is not suitable before approving Win32 packaging.

rules.title: OS compatibility is validated
rules.requirement: The application must be validated against supported Windows versions before packaging.

source.section: Application Pre-Validation / Technical Prerequisites Validation

evaluation.pass: Supported OS versions are validated.
evaluation.partial: Compatibility is assumed but not evidenced.
evaluation.fail: No OS compatibility evidence exists.

rules.remediation: Validate supported OS versions and document the result before packaging.

rules.title: Architecture compatibility is validated
rules.requirement: The application must support the required architecture. Deprecated 32-bit only applications must be reviewed carefully.

source.section: Application Pre-Validation / Technical Prerequisites Validation

evaluation.pass: Architecture is validated and aligned with the target fleet.
evaluation.partial: Architecture is known but exception review is missing.
evaluation.fail: Architecture compatibility is unknown.

rules.remediation: Document x64 or ARM64 compatibility, or open an exception review for 32-bit only apps.

rules.title: Runtime admin privileges are prohibited
rules.requirement: Applications may require elevated rights during installation, but must not require elevated rights to run after installation.

source.section: Application Pre-Validation / Technical Prerequisites Validation

evaluation.pass: Application runs without permanent admin privileges.
evaluation.partial: Admin runtime requirement is suspected but not confirmed.
evaluation.fail: Application requires permanent admin rights at runtime.

rules.remediation: Reject the package or require an approved security exception and mitigation.

rules.title: Update and patch management is documented
rules.requirement: The packaging assessment must confirm how updates are handled. Auto-update should be enabled when possible; exceptions must be justified and documented.

source.section: Application Pre-Validation / Technical Prerequisites Validation

evaluation.pass: Update model is documented and exception is justified if needed.
evaluation.partial: Update model is documented but ownership is unclear.
evaluation.fail: No update or patching model is documented.

rules.remediation: Document whether updates are automatic, manual or corporate-controlled.

rules.title: End-of-life software is not permitted
rules.requirement: Applications no longer maintained or patched by the vendor must not be packaged.

source.section: Application Pre-Validation / Technical Prerequisites Validation

evaluation.pass: Vendor support status is active.
evaluation.partial: Support status is unclear and requires confirmation.
evaluation.fail: Application is end-of-life or no longer patched.

rules.remediation: Reject the request or identify a supported replacement.

rules.title: Security licensing and data handling are validated
rules.requirement: The request must validate source legitimacy, vulnerability exposure, data handling and licensing before packaging proceeds.

source.section: Application Pre-Validation / Technical Prerequisites Validation

evaluation.pass: Security, privacy and licensing checks are documented.
evaluation.partial: Some checks are documented but approval is incomplete.
evaluation.fail: Required compliance checks are missing.

rules.remediation: Escalate to UEM, security or licensing owners before packaging.

rules.title: Installer is obtained from official vendor source
rules.requirement: Source files must be obtained from official vendor or enterprise download locations to ensure authenticity and compliance.

source.section: Sources Files / Access the official Adobe Enterprise Portal

evaluation.pass: Official source URL or vendor portal evidence is documented.
evaluation.partial: Source is plausible but not formally evidenced.
evaluation.fail: Installer source is unknown or non-official.

rules.remediation: Replace the source with an official vendor download and update package evidence.

rules.title: Version language and architecture selection are documented
rules.requirement: The selected version, language package and architecture must match the intended deployment scope.

source.section: Sources Files / Select the appropriate version

evaluation.pass: Version, language and architecture are documented.
evaluation.partial: Only some source selection attributes are documented.
evaluation.fail: Source selection attributes are missing.

rules.remediation: Document selected version, language and architecture before packaging.

rules.title: Enterprise distribution agreement is captured when required
rules.requirement: When vendor terms require an enterprise distribution agreement, evidence must be captured in the packaging documentation.

source.section: Editor Installation Instructions / EULA Handling & Distribution Agreement

evaluation.pass: Distribution agreement evidence is documented where required.
evaluation.partial: Distribution requirement is identified but evidence is incomplete.
evaluation.fail: Required distribution evidence is missing.

rules.remediation: Attach or reference vendor approval before production deployment.

rules.title: Vendor installation documentation is referenced
rules.requirement: Packaging teams must refer to official vendor documentation for current installation, update and command-line parameters.

source.section: Editor Installation Instructions / Reference Documentation

evaluation.pass: Official vendor documentation is referenced.
evaluation.partial: Documentation exists but is not linked to the package record.
evaluation.fail: No vendor documentation is referenced.

rules.remediation: Add official vendor documentation links to the package record.

rules.title: Silent EULA handling is configured
rules.requirement: The package must handle EULA acceptance silently when required by the installer.

source.section: Editor Installation Instructions / Supported Command-line Parameters

evaluation.pass: EULA is handled silently and validated.
evaluation.partial: Silent EULA handling is configured but not tested.
evaluation.fail: Installer can pause or fail due to EULA interaction.

rules.remediation: Add the vendor-supported silent EULA parameter and test installation.

rules.title: Prerequisites and dependencies are identified
rules.requirement: System-level requirements, dependencies, runtime needs and network requirements must be assessed before packaging.

source.section: Editor Installation Instructions / Pre-requisites and Dependencies

evaluation.pass: Prerequisites and dependencies are identified or explicitly not required.
evaluation.partial: Some prerequisites are documented but validation is incomplete.
evaluation.fail: Prerequisites are unknown.

rules.remediation: Document prerequisites and include dependency handling or a no-dependency statement.

rules.title: IntuneWin format is used for Intune Win32 deployment
rules.requirement: Applications deployed through the Intune Win32 app model must be packaged in IntuneWin format.

source.section: Packaging / Packaging Format

evaluation.pass: Package is built as IntuneWin for Win32 deployment.
evaluation.partial: Package format is not visible in available metadata.
evaluation.fail: Package format is inconsistent with the Intune Win32 app model.

rules.remediation: Rebuild the package using the IntuneWin preparation tool.

rules.title: Repackaging is avoided unless justified
rules.requirement: Repackaging or transformation must be avoided unless absolutely necessary.

source.section: Packaging / Packaging Format

evaluation.pass: No repackaging is used or exception is justified.
evaluation.partial: Repackaging is suspected but not documented.
evaluation.fail: Repackaging is used without justification.

rules.remediation: Prefer vendor installer parameters or document the exception.

rules.title: Package supports silent unattended SYSTEM execution
rules.requirement: Packages must install silently, unattended and be compatible with SYSTEM-context deployment.

source.section: Packaging / Packaging Format and Tools and Scripts Used

evaluation.pass: Silent unattended SYSTEM execution is validated.
evaluation.partial: Silent parameters exist but SYSTEM-context test evidence is missing.
evaluation.fail: Installation requires interaction or fails in SYSTEM context.

rules.remediation: Fix silent arguments or installer logic and retest locally.

rules.title: Custom scripts follow Sodexo constraints
rules.requirement: Custom scripts must support silent SYSTEM execution, centralized logging, naming conventions, no hardcoded credentials, modularity and local pre-testing.

source.section: Packaging / Tools and Scripts Used

evaluation.pass: Script review confirms all constraints.
evaluation.partial: Script is functional but some constraints are not evidenced.
evaluation.fail: Script violates one or more critical constraints.

rules.remediation: Refactor script to comply with Sodexo packaging constraints.

rules.title: Required packaging tools and detection approach are used
rules.requirement: Packagers must use the required packaging tools and include registry-based detection logic unless explicitly instructed otherwise.

source.section: Packaging / Tools and Scripts Used

evaluation.pass: Required tools and detection approach are followed.
evaluation.partial: Required tooling is assumed but not documented.
evaluation.fail: Package deviates without instruction or justification.

rules.remediation: Align packaging method and detection logic with the guideline or document exception.

rules.title: Standard folder structure is respected
rules.requirement: The prescribed folder structure and folder names must be followed precisely.

source.section: Packaging / Folder Structure and File Naming

evaluation.pass: Folder structure matches the packaging standard.
evaluation.partial: Minor optional content deviations are documented.
evaluation.fail: Required folders or names are missing or changed.

rules.remediation: Reorganize source package according to the standard structure.

rules.title: Detection short name is specific
rules.requirement: Detection naming must be specific enough to track the application without matching unrelated software.

source.section: Packaging / Install Uninstall Detection Logic

evaluation.pass: Detection identifier is specific and avoids unrelated products.
evaluation.partial: Detection identifier is plausible but broad.
evaluation.fail: Detection identifier is too generic and can match unrelated software.

rules.remediation: Use a specific application identifier, product code or registry path.

rules.title: ProductCode or UninstallString is preferred for MSI detection
rules.requirement: MSI-based packages should use ProductCode or UninstallString values in the uninstall registry key when applicable.

source.section: Packaging / Install Uninstall Detection Logic

evaluation.pass: Detection uses ProductCode, UninstallString or an equivalent reliable key.
evaluation.partial: Detection uses registry but not the preferred key.
evaluation.fail: MSI detection is missing or unreliable.

rules.remediation: Update detection to use MSI ProductCode or a reliable uninstall registry value.

rules.title: Binaries and scripts are placed in expected folders
rules.requirement: Binaries and scripts should be placed in expected folders. Absolute paths must be avoided unless strictly required.

source.section: Packaging / Install Uninstall Detection Logic

evaluation.pass: Files are in expected folders or exception is justified.
evaluation.partial: Absolute paths are used but appear technically required.
evaluation.fail: Absolute paths are used without justification or expected folders are not used.

rules.remediation: Move binaries/scripts to standard folders or document the exception.

rules.title: JSON configuration is syntactically valid
rules.requirement: JSON configuration must use double backslashes for paths, double quotes for strings and no unsupported comments.

source.section: Packaging / Install Uninstall Detection Logic

evaluation.pass: JSON parses successfully and path escaping is valid.
evaluation.partial: JSON parses but style issues are detected.
evaluation.fail: JSON parsing fails or contains unsupported comments.

rules.remediation: Fix JSON syntax and rerun packaging validation.

rules.title: Vendor customization tooling is preferred when available
rules.requirement: Vendor customization tooling should be used when it improves consistency and reduces reliance on post-install scripts.

source.section: Packaging / Customization

evaluation.pass: Customization is handled through vendor tooling or documented as not applicable.
evaluation.partial: Customization is handled by scripts with limited rationale.
evaluation.fail: Customization is undocumented or inconsistent.

rules.remediation: Use vendor customization tooling where appropriate or document why it is not used.

rules.title: Local installation test is mandatory
rules.requirement: The package must be tested locally before creating the IntuneWin app and uploading to Intune.

source.section: Local Testing & Validation / Installation Test

evaluation.pass: Local installation test evidence is present and successful.
evaluation.partial: Test evidence exists but is incomplete.
evaluation.fail: No local installation test evidence is available.

rules.remediation: Run local install test and document results before Intune upload.

rules.title: Local uninstallation test is mandatory
rules.requirement: The uninstallation process must be validated locally and must be silent.

source.section: Local Testing & Validation / Uninstallation Test

evaluation.pass: Silent uninstall test evidence is present and successful.
evaluation.partial: Uninstall test exists but silence or cleanup is not confirmed.
evaluation.fail: No uninstall validation exists or uninstall requires interaction.

rules.remediation: Fix uninstall command and document local uninstall test.

rules.title: Installer logs are generated in a standard location
rules.requirement: Installer and script logs should be generated and stored in a consistent predefined location for troubleshooting.

source.section: Local Testing & Validation / Log file review & return codes

evaluation.pass: Logs are generated and stored in the expected location.
evaluation.partial: Logs are generated but location or naming is inconsistent.
evaluation.fail: No installation logs are generated.

rules.remediation: Add logging parameters and standardize log output location.

rules.title: Return codes are meaningful and tested
rules.requirement: Return codes must be documented, tested and correctly surfaced in logs. Custom scripts must define meaningful return codes.

source.section: Local Testing & Validation / Log file review & return codes

evaluation.pass: Return codes are documented, tested and visible in logs.
evaluation.partial: Return codes are visible but not fully documented.
evaluation.fail: Return code behavior is unknown or inconsistent.

rules.remediation: Document return code mapping and update script exit behavior.

rules.title: Failed validation blocks progression
rules.requirement: If one or more validation points are not met, the package must be reviewed before proceeding.

source.section: Local Testing & Validation / Installation Test

evaluation.pass: All blocking validation findings are resolved before upload.
evaluation.partial: Open issues exist with accepted remediation plan.
evaluation.fail: Package proceeds despite failed validation.

rules.remediation: Stop progression and correct install command, arguments or JSON content.

rules.title: IntuneWin is created only after successful local validation
rules.requirement: The IntuneWin file must be created only after local package validation is successful.

source.section: Local Testing & Validation / IntuneWinApp Preparation

evaluation.pass: IntuneWin creation follows successful local validation.
evaluation.partial: Sequence is plausible but not evidenced.
evaluation.fail: IntuneWin is produced without validation evidence.

rules.remediation: Record validation evidence before creating or publishing the IntuneWin package.

rules.title: Local app naming convention is followed
rules.requirement: Local apps must use the naming format XX - YYY - UEM - App - CORP - WIN - {AppName}.

source.section: Intune Win32 App Setup and Packaging / App Information

evaluation.pass: Name matches the local app naming convention.
evaluation.partial: Name mostly follows convention but has minor deviations.
evaluation.fail: Name does not follow the local app naming convention.

rules.remediation: Rename the application according to the approved convention.

rules.title: Company Portal app naming convention is followed
rules.requirement: Apps published to the Company Portal must use {AppName} - XX - YYY.

source.section: Intune Win32 App Setup and Packaging / App Information

evaluation.pass: Company Portal naming convention is followed.
evaluation.partial: Name includes country/business unit but format is inconsistent.
evaluation.fail: Company Portal naming convention is not followed.

rules.remediation: Rename the published app using the Company Portal naming standard.

rules.title: Publisher uses official publisher name
rules.requirement: The Intune Publisher field must use the official publisher name.

source.section: Intune Win32 App Setup and Packaging / App Information

evaluation.pass: Publisher is populated with an official publisher name.
evaluation.partial: Publisher is populated but naming is inconsistent.
evaluation.fail: Publisher is missing or non-standard.

rules.remediation: Update Publisher using the official vendor name.

rules.title: Application version matches editor version
rules.requirement: The App Version field must be entered exactly as provided by the editor.

source.section: Intune Win32 App Setup and Packaging / App Information

evaluation.pass: Version is populated and matches source package/vendor version.
evaluation.partial: Version is populated but cannot be reconciled with source evidence.
evaluation.fail: Version is missing, generic or incorrect.

rules.remediation: Update App Version using the editor-provided version.

rules.title: Application category is filled when possible
rules.requirement: The Intune Category field should be filled when possible.

source.section: Intune Win32 App Setup and Packaging / App Information

evaluation.pass: Category is populated.
evaluation.partial: Category is missing but app is not end-user visible.
evaluation.fail: Category is missing for an app where it should be populated.

rules.remediation: Set an approved Intune category such as Productivity or Security.

rules.title: Featured app is disabled unless requested
rules.requirement: Show this as a featured app in the Company Portal must be set to No unless explicitly requested.

source.section: Intune Win32 App Setup and Packaging / App Information

evaluation.pass: Featured app is No or exception is documented.
evaluation.partial: Featured app is Yes but request evidence is unclear.
evaluation.fail: Featured app is Yes without documented request.

rules.remediation: Set featured app to No or attach an approved exception.

rules.title: Information URL uses official publisher website
rules.requirement: The Information URL should preferably use the official website of the software publisher.

source.section: Intune Win32 App Setup and Packaging / App Information

evaluation.pass: Information URL is official or not applicable.
evaluation.partial: Information URL is present but official status is not confirmed.
evaluation.fail: Information URL is missing or non-official.

rules.remediation: Update Information URL with the official publisher page.

rules.title: Privacy URL uses official publisher policy
rules.requirement: The Privacy URL should use the official privacy policy link of the publisher.

source.section: Intune Win32 App Setup and Packaging / App Information

evaluation.pass: Privacy URL points to official privacy policy or is not applicable.
evaluation.partial: Privacy URL exists but official status is not confirmed.
evaluation.fail: Privacy URL is missing or non-official.

rules.remediation: Update Privacy URL with official publisher privacy policy.

rules.title: Owner follows global or local ownership convention
rules.requirement: Global apps must use GLB - UEM as owner. Local apps must use the local entity code such as FR - UEM or UK - UEM.

source.section: Intune Win32 App Setup and Packaging / App Information

evaluation.pass: Owner is populated and follows convention.
evaluation.partial: Owner is populated but convention is inconsistent.
evaluation.fail: Owner is missing or not usable.

rules.remediation: Update Owner according to global or local ownership convention.

rules.title: Application logo follows size and format guidance
rules.requirement: Application logo should be a square image of at least 256x256 pixels in PNG or JPG format and should use the official logo when available.

source.section: Intune Win32 App Setup and Packaging / App Information

evaluation.pass: Logo meets format and official branding guidance.
evaluation.partial: Logo exists but size or source is unclear.
evaluation.fail: Logo is missing, poor quality or non-official.

rules.remediation: Upload an official square PNG or JPG logo.

rules.title: 64-bit PowerShell execution is enforced
rules.requirement: Program commands should use SysNative to ensure the 64-bit version of PowerShell is used.

source.section: Intune Win32 App Setup and Packaging / Program

evaluation.pass: Install/uninstall commands enforce 64-bit PowerShell where applicable.
evaluation.partial: Commands appear valid but PowerShell bitness is unclear.
evaluation.fail: PowerShell command can run in unintended 32-bit context.

rules.remediation: Update commands to call PowerShell through SysNative where applicable.

rules.title: Installation timeout defaults to 60 minutes unless justified
rules.requirement: Installation timeout should generally remain at 60 minutes unless a specific need exists.

source.section: Intune Win32 App Setup and Packaging / Program

evaluation.pass: Timeout is 60 minutes or exception is documented.
evaluation.partial: Timeout differs but package type may justify it.
evaluation.fail: Timeout differs significantly without justification.

rules.remediation: Reset timeout to 60 minutes or document the exception.

rules.title: User uninstall is disabled for mandatory or security apps
rules.requirement: For mandatory apps, especially security-related software or apps deployed as required, user uninstall should be set to No unless justified.

source.section: Intune Win32 App Setup and Packaging / Program

evaluation.pass: User uninstall setting is aligned with deployment criticality.
evaluation.partial: User uninstall is enabled but exception may exist.
evaluation.fail: Required or security app allows user uninstall without justification.

rules.remediation: Set user uninstall to No or document approved business exception.

rules.title: Install behavior uses system context by default
rules.requirement: System context is preferred for most apps, especially when writing to protected areas or installing for all users. User-context exceptions must be justified and tested.

source.section: Intune Win32 App Setup and Packaging / Program

evaluation.pass: Install behavior is system or exception is justified and tested.
evaluation.partial: User context is used but validation is incomplete.
evaluation.fail: User context is used with no justification.

rules.remediation: Switch to system context or document and test the exception.

rules.title: Restart behavior avoids forced reboot by default
rules.requirement: Restart behavior should default to No specific action. Forced restart options should only be used when required and validated during testing.

source.section: Intune Win32 App Setup and Packaging / Program

evaluation.pass: Restart behavior is No specific action or justified.
evaluation.partial: Restart behavior differs but technical need is plausible.
evaluation.fail: Forced restart is configured without justification.

rules.remediation: Set restart behavior to No specific action or document tested requirement.

rules.title: Standard success and reboot return codes are configured
rules.requirement: Standard Windows MSI success and reboot codes, at least 0 and 3010, must be included and ambiguous return codes avoided.

source.section: Intune Win32 App Setup and Packaging / Program

evaluation.pass: Return codes include 0 and 3010 and avoid ambiguity.
evaluation.partial: Return code configuration is present but incomplete.
evaluation.fail: Return code mapping is missing or ambiguous.

rules.remediation: Update Intune return code mapping with standard success and reboot codes.

rules.title: Architecture requirement is set appropriately
rules.requirement: For most modern applications, 64-bit only should be selected to avoid compatibility issues.

source.section: Intune Win32 App Setup and Packaging / Requirements

evaluation.pass: Architecture requirement is aligned with the application and fleet.
evaluation.partial: Architecture requirement is broad but justified by compatibility.
evaluation.fail: Architecture requirement is missing or inconsistent.

rules.remediation: Configure architecture requirement or document the exception.

rules.title: Minimum OS version excludes unsupported versions
rules.requirement: Only Microsoft-supported OS versions should be selected unless an ESU agreement exists.

source.section: Intune Win32 App Setup and Packaging / Requirements

evaluation.pass: Minimum OS version is aligned with supported OS matrix.
evaluation.partial: Minimum OS is broad but exception evidence may exist.
evaluation.fail: Unsupported OS versions are eligible without ESU evidence.

rules.remediation: Update minimum OS requirements according to UEM supported OS matrix.

rules.title: Hardware requirements remain empty unless needed
rules.requirement: Disk space, memory, logical processors and CPU speed requirements should remain empty unless a specific technical requirement exists.

source.section: Intune Win32 App Setup and Packaging / Requirements

evaluation.pass: Hardware requirements are empty or justified.
evaluation.partial: Hardware requirements are configured but may be technically justified.
evaluation.fail: Unnecessary hardware requirements may block valid devices.

rules.remediation: Remove unnecessary hardware requirements or document technical need.

rules.title: Detection rules use reliable installed-state indicators
rules.requirement: Detection rules must always be configured with reliable indicators confirming that the application is truly installed.

source.section: Intune Win32 App Setup and Packaging / Detection Rules

evaluation.pass: Detection uses reliable installed-state indicator.
evaluation.partial: Detection exists but reliability is unclear.
evaluation.fail: Detection is missing, generic or unreliable.

rules.remediation: Update detection rule using MSI product code, registry, file version or validated script.

rules.title: Detection scripts return correct exit codes
rules.requirement: Detection scripts must return exit 0 when detected and non-zero when not detected.

source.section: Intune Win32 App Setup and Packaging / Detection Rules

evaluation.pass: Detection script exit behavior is tested and correct.
evaluation.partial: Exit behavior is documented but not tested.
evaluation.fail: Detection script exit behavior is missing or incorrect.

rules.remediation: Correct detection script exit code behavior and retest.

rules.title: Detection logic is system-context safe
rules.requirement: Detection scripts run in SYSTEM context and must avoid user-specific locations unless explicitly targeting a user scenario.

source.section: Intune Win32 App Setup and Packaging / Detection Rules

evaluation.pass: Detection logic is safe for SYSTEM context.
evaluation.partial: User-specific paths exist but scenario may justify them.
evaluation.fail: Detection relies on inappropriate user-specific context.

rules.remediation: Use machine-level registry, file paths or validated user-targeted logic.

rules.title: Detection logic is specific enough
rules.requirement: Detection logic must be simple, fast, reliable and specific enough; when versions can coexist, the rule should verify version.

source.section: Intune Win32 App Setup and Packaging / Detection Rules

evaluation.pass: Detection is specific, fast and version-aware when needed.
evaluation.partial: Detection is specific but version handling is unclear.
evaluation.fail: Detection is too broad and may cause false positives.

rules.remediation: Add version-aware or product-specific detection logic.

rules.title: Dependencies are defined only when needed
rules.requirement: Dependencies should be defined when required components must be installed before the main application.

source.section: Intune Win32 App Setup and Packaging / Dependencies

evaluation.pass: Dependencies are justified or explicitly not needed.
evaluation.partial: Dependencies exist but rationale is incomplete.
evaluation.fail: Required dependencies are missing or unnecessary dependencies are configured.

rules.remediation: Add required dependencies or remove unjustified ones.

rules.title: Dependency chains are short maintained and tested
rules.requirement: Dependencies must be required, installed before the main app, up to date, and ideally limited to one or two levels.

source.section: Intune Win32 App Setup and Packaging / Dependencies

evaluation.pass: Dependencies are short, maintained and tested.
evaluation.partial: Dependencies exist but maintenance or pilot evidence is incomplete.
evaluation.fail: Long, stale or untested dependency chain exists.

rules.remediation: Reduce dependency chain and validate during pilot.

rules.title: Dependencies are not used for simple ordering logic
rules.requirement: Dependencies must not be used for simple ordering logic; script sequencing should be preferred when possible.

source.section: Intune Win32 App Setup and Packaging / Dependencies

evaluation.pass: Dependencies are used for true prerequisites only.
evaluation.partial: Ordering rationale is unclear.
evaluation.fail: Dependencies are used only for sequencing.

rules.remediation: Move simple ordering logic into the installation script.

rules.title: Supersedence is not relied on for critical global upgrades
rules.requirement: Supersedence should generally not be relied on for business-critical or global apps; version upgrades should preferably be handled directly within the package script.

source.section: Intune Win32 App Setup and Packaging / Supersedence

evaluation.pass: Upgrade model is script-controlled or supersedence use is justified.
evaluation.partial: Supersedence exists but criticality is unclear.
evaluation.fail: Critical/global app relies on supersedence without justification.

rules.remediation: Document supersedence rationale or move upgrade control into the package script.

rules.title: Final Intune review is completed before save
rules.requirement: Before saving, required fields, commands, detection rules, scope tags, restrictions and metadata must be double-checked.

source.section: Intune Win32 App Setup and Packaging / Review and Save

evaluation.pass: Final review checklist is complete.
evaluation.partial: Review is informal or not fully evidenced.
evaluation.fail: No final review evidence exists.

rules.remediation: Complete final Intune review checklist before production assignment.

rules.title: Wave-based rollout strategy is used
rules.requirement: Applications should follow a safe progressive wave-based deployment strategy for both required and available apps.

source.section: Application Deployment Strategy / Deployment Waves Overview

evaluation.pass: Pilot and production waves are visible or documented.
evaluation.partial: Wave approach exists but is incomplete.
evaluation.fail: Application is deployed broadly with no wave evidence.

rules.remediation: Create or document pilot and production assignment waves.

rules.title: Pilot validation precedes global production
rules.requirement: Global production deployment should occur only after pilot waves are validated.

source.section: Application Deployment Strategy / Deployment Waves Overview

evaluation.pass: Pilot validation evidence exists before global production assignment.
evaluation.partial: Pilot validation exists but acceptance criteria are unclear.
evaluation.fail: Global production deployment occurs without pilot validation.

rules.remediation: Run pilot and capture validation before global rollout.

rules.title: Single pilot fast path is justified
rules.requirement: A single pilot and immediate production rollout are acceptable only for simple situations where the required scope supports that choice.

source.section: Application Deployment Strategy / Deployment Waves Overview

evaluation.pass: Single pilot fast path is justified.
evaluation.partial: Fast path appears reasonable but approval is unclear.
evaluation.fail: Fast path is used with no justification.

rules.remediation: Document why single pilot is sufficient or switch to standard waves.

rules.title: Device targeting is preferred
rules.requirement: Applications should preferably be assigned to devices, not users, unless a specific scenario requires user-based targeting.

source.section: Application Deployment Strategy / Targeting Scope and Assignment Rules

evaluation.pass: Assignments are device-based or user-based exception is justified.

rules.remediation: Move assignment to device groups or document user-based targeting rationale.

rules.title: Deployment groups follow wave logic and naming conventions
rules.requirement: Required and available assignments must use the same wave logic and naming conventions.

evaluation.pass: Assignment groups follow approved naming and wave logic.

evaluation.fail: Assignment group naming or wave logic is inconsistent.

rules.remediation: Normalize assignment group names and document wave mapping.

rules.title: Teams communication is followed by email
rules.requirement: Teams communication must always be followed by an email with the same content to ensure visibility.

evaluation.pass: Teams and email communication evidence exists.

rules.remediation: Send or archive the required email communication.
